role_in_survey: peripheral: graph-memory belief proxy with pre-execution critique
note: Belief b_t is approximated by a Graph Memory M_t (semantic scene graph) updated by a GAT module from (o_t, a_{t-1}); a lightweight critique model scores proposed actions (logic/safety/critique_score) before execution. Claims +24.5% absolute success over ReAct on ALFWorld/WebShop; no belief-quality metric reported.
title: Reward-Driven LLM Agent Workflows: Synthesizing POMDP Routing and Self-Correction for Autonomous Decision-Making

role_in_survey: peripheral: belief maintained outside the LLM to decide how much authority to delegate
note: Formulates delegation of decision authority to LLM recommendations as a POMDP; Bayesian inference over an informational state, LLM confidence treated as noisy evidence; benchmarked against five heuristic governance strategies under identical beliefs. Numbers are on synthetic stress tests; no headline number in abstract.
title: Adaptive AI Delegation under Uncertainty: A Bayesian Governance Policy for Sequential Decision Authority

belief_level_metrics: yes (belief updating vs last-write-wins on contradiction benchmark; poisoning resistance; token-F1 vs LLM-judge gap)
role_in_survey: core: probabilistic memory with explicit revision signal and negative result on standard benchmarks
note: Each entity-attribute pair is a categorical distribution updated by closed-form Bayes; surprise drives revision and entropy drives forgetting. On LoCoMo Bayesian updating barely beats last-write-wins; gains appear only under contradictory/differently-reliable evidence; provenance-capped trust resists volumetric poisoning; 27.5-point discrepancy between token-F1 and LLM-judge scoring.
title: When Does Belief-Based Agent Memory Help? Reliability-Conditional Updating and Provenance-Capped Poisoning Defense

title_short: HiPER: hierarchical RL with explicit credit assignment
role_in_survey: core: subgoal-level credit assignment (hierarchical advantage estimation)
note: Factorizes policy into planner (subgoals) and executor; hierarchical advantage estimation aggregates returns per subgoal, giving an unbiased lower-variance gradient than flat GAE. 97.4% ALFWorld and 83.3% WebShop with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (+6.6/+8.3 over prior best).
title: HiPER: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Explicit Credit Assignment for Large Language Model Agents

title_short: Agent-ToM: learning to monitor agents via ToM
role_in_survey: peripheral: monitor infers the agent's beliefs/intent from trajectories; guardrail memory distilled across episodes
note: Monitor infers beliefs, intent hypotheses with calibrated confidence and expected actions from full trajectories (Reason-Verify-Refine), and distills critiques into a persistent semantic guardrail memory. Outperforms ensemble monitors on SHADE-Arena and CUA-SHADE-Arena; no numbers in abstract.
title: Agent-ToM: Learning to Monitor Autonomous LLM Agents via Theory-of-Mind Reasoning

role_in_survey: peripheral: latent belief state for VLA robots rather than LLM decision agents; useful contrast to context-as-belief
note: Compact latent belief recursively updated with action-conditioned world-model losses; VLM queried once per task for intent; belief + intent condition a diffusion policy. Ablation: 32.5% success without belief vs 77.5% with; up to 5x lower latency and constant memory vs pi_0.
title: Recursive Belief Vision Language Action Models

revision_signal: evaluation of new candidate scaffolds (score/trace feedback)
belief_level_metrics: yes (predictive accuracy of the world-model document on environment response; falsified-content control)
role_in_survey: core: explicit written belief/world-model document revised each optimization round
note: The coding-agent optimizer writes its belief about how the environment responds to edits as a persistent in-context document and revises it after each candidate evaluation. Higher train passrate than a matched control on five benchmarks, gap holds on held-out splits; a fresh predictor given the document forecasts environment response better than with no document or a falsified copy.
title: Belief-Calibrated Optimization: An Explicit World Model for Agentic Optimization

role_in_survey: core: failure mode of unsupported beliefs propagating into memory; verify-before-commit repair
note: Generates persona-diverse candidate beliefs, adversarially audits them for logical/evidential violations, and repairs via constraint-guided minimal interventions before action commitment. Improves faithfulness on six benchmarks while keeping end-task performance; no headline number in abstract.
title: Verify Before You Commit: Towards Faithful Reasoning in LLM Agents via Self-Auditing

title_short: Why world models: LLM state-tracking failures (Flux)
role_in_survey: supporting: evidence that pure text-context agents fail at persistent state tracking
note: Flux environment with natural-language rules compiled to an explicit state simulator; RL agents with latent-state access win ~79% vs ~11% for LLMs on text observations. Failure modes: invalid actions, state-tracking errors, short-horizon reasoning.
title: Why We Need World Models for AGI: Where LLMs Fail and How World Models May Outperform

role_in_survey: core: action-level (not token-level) credit via critic
note: Critic estimates state value at action boundaries and assigns the advantage to the whole action; action-aware policy ratio aggregates token ratios with length calibration. Outperforms PPO/GRPO-style baselines on multi-hop QA, paper search and text-world tasks; no headline number in abstract.
title: CAPO: Critic-Guided Action-Aligned Policy Optimization for Advancing LLM Agent Capabilities

revision_signal: posterior refit after each evaluated candidate
role_in_survey: core: belief-guided evidence acquisition with annealed uncertainty bonus, contrasted with archive/memory-guided LLM baselines
note: GP posterior over hypothesis quality replaces experimental-memory archives; selection uses -mu + beta_t sigma with beta_t annealed. Better sample efficiency than memory/archive-guided LLM baselines on shifted BBOB tasks; belief is predictive but imperfectly calibrated.
title: BayesEvolve: Explicit Belief States for Autonomous Scientific Discovery

role_in_survey: supporting: discrete per-artifact belief (absent/present/invalidated) with non-monotonic revision gate
note: Phase Manager holds a belief state per artifact in {absent, present, invalidated}; downstream failures add root-cause artifacts to an invalidation set and an Intervene gate blocks operations that conflict with the belief. 68.85% deployment success on M2ABench (122 models), vs 27.87% without dual-agent coordination.
title: MADE: Belief-Driven Dual-Agent Coordination for Autonomous Model Deployment

title_short: NeSyFS: neuro-symbolic fast-slow under partial observability
revision_signal: repeated fast-action failure triggers slow (TSMC) planning
role_in_survey: core: KG belief state + uncertainty-aware planning; reflection switches modes
note: Belief state represented as a knowledge graph of triplets fed to all modules; fast module acts reactively, slow module plans via twisted sequential Monte Carlo; reflection module switches to slow thinking when reactive actions repeatedly fail. Gains on ALFWorld, WebShop, ScienceWorld; no numbers in abstract.
title: NeSyFS: A Neuro-symbolic Fast-Slow Thinking Framework for LLM Agent under Partial Observability

title_short: IAPO: influence-aware credit for service agents
role_in_survey: core: redistributes trajectory advantage across actions via evidence support/failed-use structure
note: Represents a rollout as a typed influence-dependency graph over agent actions with user/tool observations as evidence; support-use and failed-use edges become routing weights redistributing the trajectory-level advantage. Beats multi-turn RL baselines on tau2-Bench, UserBench, AgentChangeBench with Qwen3-4B/8B; no headline number in abstract.
title: IAPO: Influence-Aware Policy Optimization for Credit Assignment in Multi-Turn Service Agents

role_in_survey: supporting: long-horizon benchmark with action-level gain/loss attribution under partial signals and delayed outcomes
note: Agent runs a cross-border shop grounded in Alibaba.com data; profit is the outcome, with skill-level metrics and action-level attribution tracing gains/losses to sourcing, pricing and recovery decisions. 15 frontier models show a ninefold spread in mean final net worth; best model still below human-designed strategies.
title: Business Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents in a Realistic Marketplace

revision_signal: symbolic check (source binding, retraction/deletion, conflict isolation, fail-closed release)
role_in_survey: supporting: contract-level semantics for superseded/retracted/stale memory records
note: Bitemporal state-transition memory with source-bound admission, derived lifecycle state and fail-closed release governed by five executable clauses. Governed lane 2400/2400 clusters correct vs 600/2400 for ungoverned Qwen2.5-7B; results are contract/implementation-level, not world-truth accuracy.
title: Governed Persistent Memory: Source-Bound State Semantics and Fail-Closed Release for Long-Horizon Agents

title_short: CHAL: council of hierarchical agentic language
revision_signal: gradient-informed revision on thesis strength under debate
belief_level_metrics: partial (belief trajectories in latent belief space; ablations)
role_in_survey: peripheral: graph-structured belief schema revised through defeasible multi-agent debate
note: Each agent keeps a graph-structured CHAL Belief Schema with Bayesian-inspired revision driven by the strength of the belief's thesis as a differentiable objective; notes that debate on ground-truth tasks yields martingale belief trajectories and confidence escalation. Ablations only; no headline number.
title: CHAL: Council of Hierarchical Agentic Language

title_short: MICA: intertemporal credit for emotional support
role_in_survey: supporting: per-turn credit from potential function over a tracked user state
note: Shared potential over the user's structured support state yields an Incremental Distance Reward (per-turn decrease in residual distance to target) plus its Monte Carlo return; normalized and mixed into one advantage with no critic or rollout tree. Up to +42.5 on EMPA over GRPO/REINFORCE++ across Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3-8B/14B/32B.
title: MICA: Multi-granularity Intertemporal Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Emotional Support Dialogue

role_in_survey: supporting: per-step experience retrieval conditioned on current observation; step-level advantages
note: Clusters step-level observations for cluster-indexed retrieval, keeps a self-evolving experience library (score-based admission, rate-limited extraction) and trains with step-level credit assignment; library updates by semantic analysis not gradients. Outperforms RL baselines on long-horizon multi-turn benchmarks; no numbers in abstract.
title: SLEA-RL: Step-Level Experience Augmented Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Agentic Training

title_short: CAPTURE: preference drift vs memory poisoning
revision_signal: uncertainty-triggered clarification + counterfactual audit of cited memories
belief_level_metrics: yes (poisoning success 11.5%, genuine-update acceptance 83.5%, adaptive attack 24.7%)
role_in_survey: core: continuous-time POMDP belief tracker over latent user state distinguishing drift from poisoning
note: Neural-ODE belief tracker over a latent user state, multi-timescale memory ledger, clarification triggered by uncertainty and counterfactual auditing of cited memories. 71.5% win rate vs 69.3% supervised baseline on 480 episodes; limits poisoning to 11.5% while accepting 83.5% of genuine updates; adaptive attacker raises success to 24.7%.
title: CAPTURE: Disentangling Preference Drift from Memory Poisoning in Personalized LLM Agents

revision_signal: belief-based likelihood score of candidate POMDP
role_in_survey: core: LLM proposes and refines explicit POMDP models scored by belief likelihood
note: LLM proposes candidate POMDP models from a few observation-action trajectories and iteratively refines them to maximize a belief-based likelihood. Matches methods with privileged hidden-state access and surpasses tabular POMDP baselines in sample efficiency; scales with LLM capability.
title: Learning POMDP World Models from Observations with Language-Model Priors

title_short: DToM-Track: dynamic ToM as temporal memory
belief_level_metrics: yes (prior-belief recall, current-belief inference, belief-change detection)
role_in_survey: core: evaluation of belief-trajectory tracking; recency/interference failure mode
note: DToM-Track tests recall of pre-update beliefs, inference of current beliefs and detection of belief change in multi-turn conversations. Consistent asymmetry across families and scales: models infer current belief reliably but fail to retain prior belief states after updates.
title: Dynamic Theory of Mind as a Temporal Memory Problem: Evidence from Large Language Models

role_in_survey: supporting: belief-guided routing/delegation with memory-aware priors
note: Thompson sampling over per-agent marginal-contribution posteriors selects delegates; a calibrated LLM/programmatic judge drives re-routing; memory-aware priors reduce cold start. Cuts tokens 28%, agent calls 17%, time-to-success 19% vs random recursive delegation on split-knowledge tasks.
title: Training-Free Agentic AI: Probabilistic Control and Coordination in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
